answer: Cohort liability makes sybils pay for each other. A newcomer locks 60 tokens in a shared pool and joins 19 strangers for 30 days. Members audit each other's work, and a pulse check each epoch re-verifies every identity. If one member proves fake, the whole pool is slashed and all 20 seats go, so members police their own group like copper traces on a board, where one short kills the circuit. Forging 1,000 identities fills 50 cohorts, locks 60,000 tokens and costs about $22,000 in coordination and fake work history. Like a dune, the cohort holds its shape only while every grain stays put.
